nodes.summary: Let $c$ map a gate literal and two operand literals to a list of clauses, and let $(a, \varphi_A, k_A)$ and $(b, \varphi_B, k_B)$ be the results for the two operands, each a literal, a clause list and a next free gate number. The step returns the positive literal $g$ of the variable $2k_B + 1$, the clause list $c(g, a, b)$ followed by $\varphi_B$, and the next free gate number $k_B + 1$. Neither $\varphi_A$ nor…
nodes.title: One step of the linear-time Tseitin builder

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, a variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ is allowed for the gate range $[k, k')$ if $x$ is even (it names an atom) or $x$ is a gate in range $[k, k')$, that is, $x = 2j + 1$ for some $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \le j < k'$.
nodes.title: Allowed variables for a gate range

nodes.summary: For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of the gate literal $g$ for the conjunction of $a$ and $b$ are, in this order, the three clauses $\lnot g \lor a$, $\lnot g \lor b$ and $g \lor \lnot a \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the complementary literal of $\ell$ (same variable, opposite polarity).
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses for a conjunction

nodes.summary: A function $f$ from assignments $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ to Booleans depends only on the atom variables if $f(\sigma) = f(\tau)$ for all assignments $\sigma$ and $\tau$ with $\sigma(2n) = \tau(2n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Functions of the atom variables

nodes.summary: Given a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, a proposition $A$ and an assignment $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$, this is the truth value of $A$ under the valuation that gives each atom $a$ the value $\sigma(2\iota(a))$.
nodes.title: Value of a proposition read off the atom variables

nodes.summary: Let the atoms have a distinguished atom $\bot$, let $\iota$ be an injective map from atoms to natural numbers and let $A$ be a proposition. The Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$, together with the unit clause making the variable $2\iota(\bot)$ false, is satisfiable if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false.
nodes.title: Equisatisfiability of the Tseitin transformation

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $A$, built from atoms with the binary connectives $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\to$, the connective count of $A$ is the number of occurrences of these connectives in $A$. It is $0$ for an atom, and for $B \circ C$, with $\circ$ one of $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\to$, it is the count of $B$ plus the count of $C$ plus $1$.
nodes.title: Connective count of a propositional formula

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ be an injective map from atoms to natural numbers, let $A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a valuation of the atoms. Then $A$ is true under $v$ if and only if some assignment $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ with $\sigma(2\iota(a)) = v(a)$ for every atom $a$ satisfies the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$.
nodes.title: Tseitin correctness

nodes.summary: For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of the gate literal $g$ for the implication from $a$ to $b$ are, in this order, the three clauses $\lnot g \lor \lnot a \lor b$, $g \lor a$ and $g \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the complementary literal of $\ell$ (same variable, opposite polarity).
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses for an implication

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, a variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ is a gate in range $[k, k')$ if $x = 2j + 1$ for some $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \le j < k'$.
nodes.title: Gate variables in a range

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ and every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every clause of the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$ has at most three literals.
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses have at most three literals

nodes.summary: For every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every formula $A$ and every gate number $k$, the list of defining clauses produced by the Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$ has length $3c$, where $c$ is the number of binary connectives of $A$.
nodes.title: Number of defining clauses in the Tseitin encoding

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ and every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$, as a list of clauses counted with repetition, has length $3c + 1$, where $c$ is the number of binary connectives of $A$: three defining clauses per connective plus the unit clause asserting $A$.
nodes.title: Number of clauses of the Tseitin CNF

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign a Boolean value to every natural-number variable, and let $\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal with variable $x$ and polarity $b$. The truth value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ is true exactly when $\sigma(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Truth value of a literal

nodes.summary: The complement of a literal $(x, b)$ with variable $x$ and polarity $b$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: the same variable with the opposite polarity.
nodes.title: Complementary literal

nodes.summary: For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of the gate literal $g$ for the disjunction of $a$ and $b$ are the three clauses $\lnot g \lor a \lor b$, $g \lor \lnot a$ and $g \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the complementary literal of $\ell$.
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses for a disjunction

nodes.summary: For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables and all CNF formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $\sigma$ satisfies the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$ followed by those of $\psi$ if and only if $\sigma$ satisfies both $\varphi$ and $\psi$.
nodes.title: Satisfying a concatenation of CNF formulas

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be assignments of Boolean values to the natural-number variables that agree on every variable occurring in a literal of $\varphi$. If $\sigma$ satisfies $\varphi$, then $\tau$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ map atoms to natural numbers, let $A$ be a proposition and $k$ a natural number, and let $(\ell, \Phi, k')$ be the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$: the literal naming $A$, its defining clauses and the next unused gate number. For an assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables, let $A[\sigma]$ be the truth value of $A$ when each atom $a$ gets the…
nodes.title: Correctness invariant of the Tseitin encoding

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $r = (\ell, \Phi, k')$ consist of a literal $\ell$, a CNF formula $\Phi$ and a natural number $k'$, and let $v$ map each assignment of Boolean values to the natural-number variables to a Boolean value. Call a variable a gate in range if it equals $2j + 1$ for some $j$ with $k \le j < k'$. The invariant holds for $k$, $r$ and $v$ when $k \le k'$; the variable of $\ell$ and every…
nodes.title: Tseitin encoding invariant

nodes.summary: For every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every formula $A$, every gate number $k$ and every clause list $\mathit{acc}$, the linear-time Tseitin builder run on $A$ from gate $k$ with accumulator $\mathit{acc}$ returns the same literal naming $A$ and the same next unused gate number as the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$, and its clause list is $X$ followed by $\mathit{acc}$…
nodes.title: The linear-time Tseitin builder agrees with the reference encoding

nodes.summary: Fix a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers. Given a formula $A$, a gate number $k$ and a clause list $\mathit{acc}$, the builder returns a literal naming $A$, a clause list and the next unused gate number. For an atom $a$ it returns the positive literal of variable $2\iota(a)$, the list $\mathit{acc}$ unchanged, and $k$. For $A \circ B$ with $\circ$ one of $\wedge$, $\vee$, $\to$, it runs on $A$ from gate $k$…
nodes.title: Linear-time Tseitin builder

nodes.summary: Fix a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers. Given a formula $A$ and a gate number $k$, the encoding returns a literal naming $A$, a list of defining clauses and the next unused gate number. For an atom $a$ it returns the positive literal of variable $2\iota(a)$, no clauses, and $k$. For $A \circ B$ with $\circ$ one of $\wedge$, $\vee$, $\to$, it encodes $A$ from gate $k$, obtaining a literal $a$, clauses $C_A$…
nodes.title: Tseitin encoding with gates numbered from $k$

nodes.summary: For an atom type with a distinguished atom $\bot$, a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and a formula $A$, this is the CNF consisting of the unit clause whose literal is the negative literal of variable $2\iota(\bot)$, followed by the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$.
nodes.title: Tseitin CNF with $\bot$ false

nodes.summary: For every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and every formula $A$, the Tseitin CNF of $A$ is the unit clause whose literal is the literal naming $A$ in the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $0$, followed by a list of clauses that is a permutation of the defining clauses of that encoding.
nodes.title: The Tseitin CNF reorders the reference encoding

nodes.summary: Given a rule $\mathit{cl}$ assigning to literals $g$, $a$, $b$ a list of defining clauses, and the results $(a, C_A, k_A)$ and $(b, C_B, k_B)$ of encoding the two operands of a binary connective (each a literal, a clause list and a next unused gate number), the step returns the positive literal $g$ of variable $2k_B+1$, the clause list $C_A$, then $C_B$, then $\mathit{cl}(g, a, b)$, and the next gate number $k_B+1$.
nodes.title: One step of the Tseitin encoding

nodes.summary: For a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and a formula $A$, run the linear-time Tseitin builder on $A$ with gates numbered from $0$ and the empty accumulator, obtaining a literal $\ell$ naming $A$ and a clause list $C$. The Tseitin CNF of $A$ is the unit clause $[\ell]$ followed by $C$.
nodes.title: Tseitin CNF
Logic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
